chunks.text: The switch statement is used to perform different actions based on different conditions.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: Here is the basic syntax.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: First, the switch expression gets evaluated.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: Then the value of the expression is compared with the values of each case.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: If there is a match, the associated block of code is executed.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: If there is not a match, then the default block of code will run.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: When JavaScript reaches a break keyword, it breaks out of the switch block.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: Note that if you omit the break statement, the next case will be executed even if the

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: evaluation does not match the case.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: Here is an example.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: In our expression, we are using the getDay method which returns the weekday as a number

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: between 0 and 6, 0 being Sunday.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: We can now use case to compare our value.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: If it is 0, then day will equal Sunday.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: If it is 1, then day will equal Monday.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement
chunks.text: And so on.

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement

chunks.title: JavaScript Switch Statement

text: The switch statement is used to perform different actions based on different conditions. Here is the basic syntax. First, the switch expression gets evaluated. Then the value of the expression is compared with the values of each case. If there is a match, the associated block of code is executed. If there is not a match, then the default block of code will run. When JavaScript reaches a break keyword, it breaks out of the switch block. Note that if you omit the break statement, the next case will be executed even if the evaluation does not match the case. Here is an example. In our expression, we are using the getDay method which returns the weekday as a number between 0 and 6, 0 being Sunday. We can now use case to compare our value. If it is 0, then day will equal Sunday. If it is 1, then day will equal Monday. And so on. At the end of each block, we include a break, since we do not want any code to run after we have found a match. In this example, we use multiple case statements to execute blocks of code. So if the day is 4 or 5, which would be Thursday or Friday, we want to say, it's almost the weekend. If that isn't true, then we'll check to see if the day is 0 or 6, which is Saturday or Sunday. If so, then we'll say, it's the weekend. And if that isn't true, then we'll use the default code block and say, looking forward to the weekend. This has been a 90-second JavaScript January.
